There are 4 reduced Latin squares of order 4. Each Latin square can be reduced by permuting its rows and columns so that the first row and first column are 1,2,3,4. Conversely, each reduced square yields 4! choices for the row permutation and 3! choices for the remaining column permutation, so the total is 4 · 4! · 3! = 576. An explicit reduced-square construction is the cyclic square
1 2 3 4
2 3 4 1
3 4 1 2
4 1 2 3.
The other three reduced squares are obtained by replacing the symbols 2,3,4 in the last three rows according to the three non-equivalent reduced arrangements; direct enumeration gives exactly 4 reduced squares. Thus the count of all squares is 576.
